ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Maja decided to enter numbers into the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid. She wanted to do this in such a way that the numbers in each of the four $2 \times 2$ grids that form part of the $3 \times 3$ grid have the same totals. She has already written numbers in three of the corner cells, as shown in the diagram. Which number does she need to write in the bottom right corner?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a 3 by 3 grid with corner entries: top-left = 3, top-right = 1, bottom-left = 2, bottom-right = x. Label the remaining cells arbitrarily, for example top-middle = b and bottom-middle = h. From the text, all four 2 by 2 subgrids have the same total. Equate the top-left 2 by 2 block with the bottom-left 2 by 2 block; the shared middle-row entries cancel, giving 3 + b = 2 + h. Equate the top-right 2 by 2 block with the bottom-right 2 by 2 block; shared middle-row entries cancel, giving b + 1 = h + x. Subtract or combine these two equations: from 3 + b = 2 + h, h = b + 1; then b + 1 = h + x gives x = 0.

method.method_draft: View the four 2 by 2 totals as a sliding window condition. In the top two rows, sliding the 2 by 2 window from the left position to the right position must not change the sum, so the two cells that leave the window, including the top-left 3 and the middle-left cell, must have the same total as the two cells that enter, including the top-right 1 and the middle-right cell: 3 + L = 1 + R. In the bottom two rows, the same left-to-right slide gives 2 + L = x + R, where x is the bottom-right value. Subtract the second slide equation from the first: (3 + L) - (2 + L) = (1 + R) - (x + R), so 1 = 1 - x, hence x = 0.
